page: Vultr vx1-g-96c-384g is a general-purpose cloud compute instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute product family. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD processor architecture offering 96 dedicated virtual CPU cores. Memory capacity is provisioned at 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The configuration operates without discrete graphics processing units.

Storage provisions for the instance include 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Given the minimal local disk allocation relative to the extensive 96-core compute footprint, data-intensive storage workflows require external network or block storage attachments. The dedicated allocation of 96 AMD vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of system memory provides high resource density for multi-threaded applications while maintaining operational cost efficiency for large-scale enterprise deployments.

This server profile is structured for CPU-intensive, horizontally parallel, and memory-balanced enterprise workloads. Suitable applications include large-scale web serving tiers, software compilation farms, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, extract-transform-load (ETL) processing, and container orchestration clusters requiring dedicated core scheduling.
